chitchat: Wendel turns a bolt over, finds the thread he wants, and drops it into a paper bag without looking.
"If it moves and it shouldn't, tape. If it should move and it doesn't, oil. That's the whole trade."
Somewhere in the back, something is cut, and the smell of hot steel drifts through.
description: A wide, unhurried man in a canvas apron with a pencil behind each ear, one for wood and one for metal, and he will tell you which is which if you ask. He has never once said a thing couldn't be fixed. He has, several times, said it wasn't worth fixing, which he considers a completely different sentence.

root.text: Wendel looks you over the way he'd look over a bracket. "Right. What's broken, or what are you about to break?" He sets down a pencil. "Either's fine. I stock for both."

options.label: Can you fix things, or just sell parts?
What's the chalk argument on the back wall?

fix.text: "I sell parts. Watts up at the turbine hall does benches." He taps a drawer. "What I'll do is tell you which of these you actually need, which is usually the cheaper one, and that's why I'm still here and the place before me isn't."

chalk.text: He doesn't turn round. "Fella says a thing's fixed when it works. I say a thing's fixed when it works without you." A long pause. "He's been winning for about a year, which tells you something about the year."

gossip.text: "People tell you things while you're counting screws. I don't think they notice they're doing it."

bye.text: "Mind the stock under the awning. It bites at the ankle."

clothing_layers: a heavy canvas apron gone black at the pockets
a flannel work shirt with the cuffs rolled past the burn scars
thick work trousers and plain shorts

name: Wendel Corry
